correctness.rationale: For a nonempty subquandle S, composites of right reflections translate by 2(y−z). These translations generate exactly the subgroup H generated by differences, since doubling is invertible on finite odd-order H, proving S=a+H. For U=a+H and V=b+K, write M=H+K. Disjointness means b−a is outside M and the join is a+(M+⟨b−a⟩). Both conditions hold exactly when b−a+M generates a nontrivial cyclic A/M. Each generator has [M:K] lifts as K-cosets, yielding the coefficient at fixed K. In the cyclic case M has index g=gcd(d,e), and [M:K]=e/g. The unrestricted local sum at p dividing d, with p^α exactly dividing n, is p^α (sum the totient at exponents up to v_p(d), then a geometric sum); off that support it is σ(p^α). Excluding g=1 subtracts exactly σ(n/P_d(n)). In C3×C9, for H0 the three other order-three subgroups and all four order-nine subgroups contribute 6z³ and 2z⁹ apiece. For H1 the trivial K contributes 18z, each of the four order-three K contributes 6z³, and only the elementary abelian order-nine K contributes 2z⁹. This checks both profiles. The scope excludes the empty and whole quandle. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed; the proof and example do not require empirical extrapolation.

value.rationale: Beyond existence, the exact profile is an invariant of the embedding of a subquandle in its lattice. The C3×C9 comparison distinguishes equal-order, abstractly isomorphic subquandles; the cyclic total reduces the count to prime support while the profile retains size information. These consequences make the exact count useful in the canonical odd affine family, rather than a single unmotivated finite census.
residual_risks: The general formula still requires subgroup data; it is not a universal closed product for all finite abelian A.
